last_concept_check: Concept 57 'In Your wrath, remember mercy' is the theme's own words of hope (Hab 3:2 with Ps 30:5, Isa 12:1, Isa 54:7-8, Lam 3:31-32, Mic 7:9, 7:18, Jas 2:13), every passage from within the theme, and nothing in it is softened: 'a surge of anger', 'I must endure the rage of the LORD' and 'judgment without mercy' are kept whole. The dark is not displaced to make room: wrath, the day of wrath, weeping and gnashing, eternal fire, the lake of fire and the way of the wicked each keep a concept of their own. Accepted. One thinness: the closing concept has a single New Testament passage (Jas 2:13, which is half warning); see 'missing' for the New Testament's own words of hope.

concepts.why: Every passage names God as Judge. Note: concept 2 below says the same thing and should merge into this one.

note_fixes: Psalm 96:13: if concept 2 is kept apart, it is word for word the same line as 1 Chronicles 16:33 and (in part) Psalm 98:9, which sit under concept 56. Preferred fix: merge Psalm 9:7-8, 58:11, 82:8 and 96:13 into concept 1 (no ceiling on size).
concepts.why: Same sub-theme named twice. Concept 1 ('God is Judge of the earth', Ps 94:2, 75:7, 50:6) and concept 2 ('God judges the earth', Ps 58:11, 82:8, 96:13) carry the same claim, and 94:2 and 82:8 are nearly the same sentence. Also, the name says 'in righteousness' but Ps 58:11 and 82:8 do not say righteousness (82:8 is a plea, not a statement). Merge into 1, or if kept rename 'A God who judges the earth' (Ps 58:11). Reader: secular/literary - a name that outruns two of its four passages.

Biblical-theological / secular reader: the name is 'I will show My holiness', a statement that holiness is shown in judgment. Isa 6:3 (the seraphim's praise) and 6:5 (the prophet's undoing) are a vision of holiness; neither verse says anything is judged or shown by judgment, so they share the word 'holy' only. Lev 10:2-3, Isa 5:16, Ezek 28:22 and 38:23 hold the concept; Hab 1:13 may stay as the objection that the pure God seems to tolerate evil. Five passages remain.
Minor: Ezek 22:29 states the charge only, with no judgment in the verse; consider extending to 22:29-31, where the indignation is poured out. Isa 10:1-2 and Jer 22:13 are woes, which is acceptable.
Deut 24:16 / Ezek 18 set beside Exod 20:5 (concept 5) with no line reconciling them is the right handling.

Eastern Orthodox / Catholic / Reformed / Wesleyan / secular and Jewish readers: Gen 2:17 and 3:19 under a concept with Rom 5:12 makes Genesis 2-3 the origin of death for all people, which is exactly where traditions part (ancestral sin vs inherited guilt vs 'Genesis does not say this'), and Genesis itself does not say it. Rom 6:23 ('the wages of sin is death') stays and says what the name needs; Rom 5:12 can go to the Sin/Exile/Death theme.

concepts.name: It is time for judgment to begin
concepts.why: Baptist/dispensational, Jewish, Catholic, Reformed readers: 'the family of God' (1 Pet 4:17) over Amos 3:2, Jer 25:29 and Ezek 9:6 says Israel and the church are the same people, which is the Israel-and-church question. 'It is time for judgment to begin' (1 Pet 4:17's own first clause) fits Ezek 9:6 ('begin at My sanctuary') and Jer 25:29 ('I am beginning') without naming who is meant. Keep the four passages.
Close to concept 24 (Jer 50:29 'Repay her according to her deeds; do to her as she has done' says both), but the two lines are different claims (deeds vs like for like); keep apart.
Concept 29 overlaps this one heavily; see 'duplicates'.
Zeph 1:14-15 is one passage split between 27 and 29; see 'duplicates'.
Matthew 23:33 ('How will you escape the sentence of hell?') has no home elsewhere once removed from concept 45; it is a question of the same kind as Mal 3:2 and Ps 130:3 and can be added here.
Minor: Isa 34:2 says anger, not gathering; extending to Isa 34:1-2 ('Draw near, O nations') makes it say what the name says.

concepts.name: Coming with His angels and His holy ones
note_fixes: Jude 1:14-15: the ellipsis is not needed; the two halves are continuous (only the verse number falls between). Use: Behold, the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones to execute judgment on everyone
concepts.why: Name against passages: three of seven passages say 'angels' (Matt 25:31, Mark 8:38, 2 Thess 1:7), the rest 'holy ones' or 'saints'; whether the holy ones are angels or the saints is a point where Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed and dispensational readers part, so the name should carry both words and no more. Deut 33:2 is the Lord's coming at Sinai in the past; nothing in the verse is judgment.

Catholic, Orthodox vs Protestant readers: Heb 9:27 ('after that to face judgment') says judgment follows death, with no day; under 'The day of judgment' it reads as the one general day, whereas the particular judgment at death is the very point where the order of the last things divides. Move it to concept 35, which does not name a time.

note_fixes: Hebrews 9:27: add here (moved from concept 34). Note: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment
concepts.why: Matt 25:19 is the master settling accounts inside a parable; it does not say God's judgment seat (it names no judge but the master). It is already carried by 'The sheep and the goats'/'Much will be required' territory, so it need not be here.

concepts.name: Found written in the book
note_fixes: Daniel 7:10: extend the passage to 7:10-11 (court convened, books opened, the beast slain and thrown into the blazing fire), the home for Dan 7:11 removed from concept 46. Keep the note on 7:10 as it is.
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'books were opened' is said only by Dan 7:10 and Rev 20:12; Exod 32:33, Ps 69:28, Dan 12:1, Mal 3:16, Rev 3:5 and 20:15 are about a name being written in or blotted from the book, which is what they have in common with 20:12. Dan 12:1 ('found written in the book') names all of it in the texts' words.
Name is Acts 24:15's own words. Rev 20:5-6 is rightly left out; the concept sets the four passages side by side without saying one resurrection or two.

Optional note change: Matt 13:30's note 'Let both grow together until the harvest' is the clause least about separating; 'First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.' says what the name says.

note_fixes: John 15:6: extend the passage to 15:5-6; verse 6 alone has no fruit in it, which the name requires, and 15:5 supplies it ('bears much fruit').
concepts.why: Name against passages: John 15:6 says 'does not remain in Me' and fire, but not fruit. Extending to 15:5-6 fixes that without saying who the branches are (a point where Calvinist and Arminian readers part).

Secular/Jewish reader of Job: in Job 21 the question is rhetorical and Job's answer is that the wicked are NOT swept away (21:7-17); read alone under 'Like chaff driven off by the wind' it says the opposite of Job's argument. The verse belongs with the wicked who prosper (see 'missing'). Six passages remain.

note_fixes: Matthew 7:13: add (the road that leads to destruction)
Matthew 10:28: add here as well as concept 47 (fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell)
concepts.why: Hell and its duration, the point where Reformed, Wesleyan, Baptist, Catholic, Orthodox and Pentecostal readers divide. Concepts 44, 45 and 46 carry the unending-torment words ('forever and ever', 'never quenched', 'eternal punishment') in 20 passages; this concept is the only home of the 'perish/destroy' words, and its strongest New Testament lines (Matt 10:28, Matt 7:13, Phil 3:19) are missing or buried in 'Fear God'. Without them the two sets are not side by side on equal weight. Ps 1:6, 37 and 73:27 are this-life statements; the concept does not say otherwise, which is right.

Name against passages: Matt 23:33 ('the sentence of hell') mentions no fire. Move it, do not lose it: it fits concept 30 as a question ('How will you escape...?'). Matt 5:22 'the fire of hell' stays; it is not stated eternal but is the text's own word for the place.

Name against passages: Dan 7:11 has 'blazing fire', not a lake, and putting it with Revelation's beast says the beast of Daniel is the beast of Revelation, which Jewish and secular readers (and most traditions) do not agree on. Move it by extending Dan 7:10 to 7:10-11 in concept 36 so the scene stays whole. Rev 2:11 (second death) can stay since 20:14 and 21:8 define it.

Ps 82:1-3 is addressed to 'the gods' in the divine assembly; the concept's name does not say who they are, which is right (human judges, divine beings, and the Jewish and Christian readings differ). Do not describe them in any note.

note_fixes: Psalm 98:8-9: the ellipsis joins two clauses and is not an exact quotation of the verse. Use the continuous clause of verse 9: for He comes to judge the earth
concepts.why: Note fix only. Also see concept 2: 1 Chr 16:33, Ps 96:13 and Ps 98:9 are the same line, split between two concepts.

duplicates: Concepts 1 and 2 are the same sub-theme named twice (God is the Judge of the earth / God judges the earth); Ps 94:2 and Ps 82:8, and Ps 96:13 and 1 Chr 16:33 (concept 56), say the same thing. Merge 2 into 1.

Concepts 27 (The Day of the LORD) and 29 (The day of wrath) are nearly one: Zeph 1:14 and 1:15 are one passage split in two, Ezek 7:19 and Lam 2:22 are 'the Day of the LORD' in other words. Each name is the texts' own, so this is a judgment call, but a reader opening both will meet the same day twice; merging them is permitted (no ceiling) and would be a smaller outline.
Concepts 23 and 24 (repay according to deeds / as you have done) and concepts 51 and 52 (God saves the lowly / the psalmist asks to be vindicated) are close but make different claims; keep apart.
secondary_or_links: Links: restore 'Sacrifice' (or the nearest theme) - Exod 12:13 and 12:23 ('when I see the blood, I will pass over you') are already in this outline and the 'blood on the doorframe' secondary, and judgment-and-blood is a thread the Reformed, Lutheran and Orthodox readers will look for. This is a link only, with no claim made.
Secondary 'Judgment -> Comfort' repeats Isa 12:1, which is also in concept 57; harmless, but one of the two could use another passage (Isa 40:1-2 alone is enough).

Order of concepts 31-46: they read as a sequence (gathered, coming, judge, seat, books, resurrection, separation, sheep and goats, fates). The order is not a standard one (books come before resurrection, the coming after the gathering), which is what keeps it from taking a side between one judgment and several, but a reader will take it as a story. The simplest safeguard: keep 'Matthew 25:32' in both 31 and 39 only if both are wanted; and do not add Rev 20:5-6 or 1 Thess 4:16 here, as the drafter rightly left them out.
Concept 38 'Gen 18:25' also sits under concept 1; overlap is welcome, no change.

missing.sub_theme: The saints will judge the world
missing.why: The texts say the holy ones themselves sit in judgment and will judge angels; a plain sub-theme under Judgment. Rev 20:4 left out on the same ground as Rev 20:6.

missing.sub_theme: The winepress of the wrath of God
missing.why: The harvest and winepress images of the last judgment are among the darkest in the texts and are not in the outline.

The New Testament's own words of hope in this theme. The outline has John 3:36 and Rom 2:5 but not this; the hope concept has one New Testament line. Lutheran and Reformed readers will notice. Should come before concept 57 or be added inside it. John 3:18 can sit beside it as the dark half.

missing.sub_theme: The LORD is slow to anger
missing.why: The texts put patience and 'will by no means leave the guilty unpunished' in the same sentence; this is the root of the judgment-and-mercy strand and of the 'how long' concept.

missing.sub_theme: Why does the way of the wicked prosper?
missing.why: The counter-question to judgment, which the texts press as hard as judgment itself; also a home for Job 21:18 removed from concept 42.
The refused-at-the-door passages, among the darkest in the Gospels, absent from an outline that otherwise keeps its dark; they also close the gap between 'Fear God' and the sheep and goats.
